tier: v1 legacy per-purchase policy snapshot tier (not the reviewed merchant-pack tier, R01 v2)
construction: Constructed by hand by opus-rules-researcher (M02, task M1C) on 2026-09-23 from the R01 spec (§1.4, §4, L1) and the R01 v1 behaviour specified in contract rev 4 (044b20d) §2.7 and §10, D145, and DA-A-2 / DA-A-13 / DA-A-22 / DA-A-33. No new R01 v1 evaluator exists yet (M12), and none was consulted. Legacy parity values (the drop threshold, 24-hour-multiple window arithmetic, observation rejection bars) were cross-checked against TODAY's legacy behaviour in convex/lib/ledger.ts (priceDropCents, windowEndsAt) and convex/priceWatch.ts (recordCheck, rejectionReason, implausiblyCheap) at 044b20d. That code is the parity reference, not the code under test. `legacy_note` values are informative strings from that path; an evaluator is not required to emit them.

conventions.fact_encoding: facts.<key> = {type, value, state}; state in {user_confirmed, observed, derived, extracted_candidate, conflicting, missing, assumption} (README 'Fixture format'); an accepted price observation is `observed` (contract §2.5 legacy adapter). Fact keys follow contract §2.7: retail.purchase_date, retail.unit_price, retail.quantity, retail.observed_price, retail.window_days, retail.policy_confirmed, retail.policy_temporal, retail.currency. money = {amount_minor:int, currency:ISO-4217}. datetime = ISO-8601 with offset.
conventions.observation: An observation is accepted only if it is a single price (not a range), > 0, variantMatch 'exact', currency equal to the purchase currency, confidence >= 0.7, and not implausibly cheap (>= round(10% of the unit price paid)). A rejected observation never becomes retail.observed_price.
conventions.threshold: A drop qualifies when (unit_price - observed) >= max(100 minor units, round(2% of unit_price)). The claim amount is (unit_price - observed) x quantity.
conventions.after_settled_claim: If confirmed (paid) price-adjustment claims on the item total S > 0, the new ask is (drop x qty) - S, and it opens only if that remainder >= max(100, round(2% of unit_price x quantity)). Each ask is a new loss key (n+1).
conventions.window: Legacy window end = purchasedAt + windowDays x 86,400,000 ms (24-hour multiples from the purchase instant, contract HC-11 / O15), NOT calendar days. Auto-open is allowed while now <= windowEndsAt. After windowEndsAt no new claim auto-opens. Sending an existing claim after windowEndsAt is NOT refused: it requires the acknowledgment `window_may_have_passed` (D145 DA-A-21/O14).
conventions.best_outcome: R01 v1's best outcome is likely_eligible (fixture alias likely_eligible_missing_evidence), never eligible. retail.policy_temporal is always present in v1 (A-T1 or A-T2), per contract §2.7.
conventions.assumption_class: retail.policy_confirmed, retail.policy_temporal and retail.currency (legacy currency not confirmed, DA-A-33) are assumption-class. They appear in expected.assumptions, never in expected.missing_facts, and never block a claim (DA-A-2).
conventions.temporal_assumptions: A-T1 = policy snapshot retrieved within +/-7 days of purchasedAt ('policy text retrieved within a week of your purchase; assumed to be the policy then'). A-T2 = otherwise ('retrieved N days after purchase; the policy may have changed'; next action 'refresh policy'). Contract §2.7 does not say whether exactly 7 days counts as 'within'; no case tests that instant.
conventions.staleness: R01 v1 has no external-source refresh window (D145 d): freshness is measured against the purchase date and only adds an assumption. Unlike R02-11 / R03-10 / R04-10 / R05-11, no R01 case expects source_unverified for staleness. R01-11 is the stale-snapshot case, and it is assumption-only.
conventions.claim_block: expected.claim = {opens: bool, amount, windowEndsAt, loss_key_note?, legacy_note?}. opens=false with outcome likely_eligible means the evaluation qualifies but the legacy guard (open claim, already settled) prevents a second claim.
conventions.loader: Same as R02-R05: a case has EITHER a top-level `expected` OR an `expected` on every variant; `clock`/`source` may be on the case or the variant (variant wins); `facts_from` + `facts_override` copy another case's facts; a variant's `change` replaces the named facts; `context_change` replaces named context entries. `action` defaults to 'evaluate'; 'send_existing_claim' (R01-05d) exercises the send path (M13 drafts.prepareSend/approveAndSend) and carries expected.send in addition to the outcome. `context` holds non-fact state (existing claims on the item, ShopSavvy history, unconfirmed offers).
conventions.conflicting: A conflicting fact carries `candidates`. If the candidates give different outcomes → needs_facts and no claim. If every candidate gives the same outcome, the conflict is not material: outcome likely_eligible and the claim's windowEndsAt uses the EARLIEST candidate (README cross-pack rule 3).

cases.title: Drop threshold boundary: 2% tier and $1 floor tier

justification.reasoning: Threshold = max(100, round(unit x 2%)): 400 for a 20,000 item, 100 (the $1 floor) for a 3,000 item. A drop exactly at the threshold qualifies.

cases.title: Unconfirmed policy snapshot + qualifying drop → still likely_eligible and exactly one claim

forbidden_outputs: retail.policy_confirmed listed as a missing required fact

justification.reasoning: Today an unconfirmed policy still opens a claim. retail.policy_confirmed is assumption-class and does not set factsKnown, so the outcome is likely_eligible and the claim opens (parity).

passages: contract HC-11 and O15 (24 h multiples in R01 v1)
contract §10 R01 ('window + 1 minute → warning with acknowledgment, not a refusal')
justification.reasoning: The legacy window ends at an instant, not at a calendar day. Opening stops after it; sending an already-open claim after it needs an explicit acknowledgment and is never hard-refused.
